---
title: "Fixed quantile tiers"
subtitle: "3.1 · a simulated league, after the postrank theory book, ch. 9, 16 and 17"
description: "Posterior evaluation of directions stated by quantile groups of the estimates."
---

A quantile-tier rule sorts units by their estimates and divides them into groups of nearly equal size. It places
every unit in a higher tier above every unit in a lower tier and leaves pairs in the same tier unranked. The rule
uses the estimates to make these assignments. We use a posterior distribution to assess how often the directions
would be wrong and how much the report would cost if withholding also carries a penalty.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Three tiers.** Three groups of 10 state 300 of 435 pairs, a share of .690. Under the teaching posterior they
  expect 51.86 wrong directions, .173 per stated direction, and risk .1813 at τ .20. The marks identify all stated pairs with error above τ, including comparisons across several boundaries.
- **Ten tiers, marks on.** Disclosure rises to 405 pairs (.931), but expected wrong directions rise to 89.40 and
  E/N to .221. There are 197 marked pairs; the largest stated error is .802. At this τ, the tier rule has risk .2193, compared with .2000 if it withholds every direction. Here τ sets the cost of withholding.
- **Four tiers.** Quantile positions produce sizes 8, 7, 8, 7 and state 337 pairs (.775). The grouped formula counts within-tier withheld pairs. The equal-size closed form disappears because four does not divide thirty.
- **Two tiers.** Groups of 15 state 225 pairs (.517). The triangles in the pair map mark comparisons within a tier. Use the arrow keys to read individual cells.
- **Thirty tiers.** Every pair is stated. The tiers follow the estimates, so their 102.2 expected wrong directions
  differ from the 94.48 of the posterior-mean ranking in [Ranking states many claims](../uncertainty/ranking-claims.qmd).
  With G set to one, E/N becomes “NA: no disclosure,” while risk is .2000.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The example uses one set of estimates for thirty simulated units and independent normal posteriors based on a prior
with mean 0 and SD .15. A change in τ changes the reporting loss and which errors the app marks. The estimates
still determine tier membership. If an exact tie spans two tiers, postrank merges those tiers to keep the tied units together.
:::
